Kybartai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Marijampolė County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Kybartai's Jewish community developed alongside the town itself, which grew from the construction of a Russian railway connecting to the European network around 1865; the community enjoyed relatively high living standards for the Pale of Settlement, and wealthier families sent children to German-language schools across the border, gradually 'Germanizing' their Yiddish. The town was the birthplace of Isaac Levitan (1861–1900), one of Russia's greatest landscape painters, whose work hangs in major Russian museums and the Israel Museum in Jerusalem. Until 1912, Kybartai's Jews had no cemetery of their own and buried their dead in nearby Virbalis; a Chevra Kadisha founded that year finally obtained a plot outside town. All 1,300 of Kybartai's Jews were murdered alongside the Jews of Virbalis between July and September 1941.
